newsitem.title: USA: Most NYS voters favor keeping rent controls - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most NYS voters favor keeping rent controls - poll.

text.p: Most New York State residents want Albany to keep rent controls, which the state Senate wants to eliminate, but most of the support for the system was concentrated in New York City, a new poll said Tuesday.

New York City has the vast majority of the apartments that are covered by rent controls, and the controversy over these regulations was expected to be a major obstacle to efforts to reach a fiscal 1998 budget on time, as the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, is a Manhattan Democrat.
New York State Gov George Pataki, who last year set a national record for late budgets, proposed separating issues that do not have a fiscal impact from the budget, so they could be dealt with later.

"I would imagine there are some of the issues that don't have fiscal implications that could be deferred, and I'd be willing to do that if it looked like we had the ability to achieve a budget on time," he told reporters in Albany. The governor did not identify any specific issues.

New York State residents favor keeping the rent rules by a 54 percent majority, but 30 percent would support gradually phasing out the regulations, and nine percent would immediately end them, according to a Quinnipiac College poll.
In New York City, however, 62 percent want the system to continue, with 25 percent favoring a phase-out and 10 percent backing ending the system.
The poll survyed 1,071 New Yorkers, who said they were registered voters, from February 2 to March 2, and has a margin of error of plus or minus three percent.
